idiom_name: gorilla/securecookie (HMAC-authenticated, optionally AES-encrypted) over net/http cookies
implementation_notes: Go's standard library provides only the carrier - http.Cookie, http.SetCookie and Request.Cookie - so the codec comes from a library: gorilla/securecookie encodes and decodes authenticated (HMAC, hash key required) and optionally AES-encrypted (block key) cookie values, with EncodeMulti/DecodeMulti giving key rotation for free. Because the codec is a plain value, keep it behind a small interface and let handlers work with a typed struct rather than map[string]string. Two choices must be made deliberately: the serializer (gob, which needs gob.Register for custom types, or the built-in JSON encoder) and the key source (strong keys from GenerateRandomKey are not persisted by themselves - store them in configuration or a secret manager, and remember that restarting with fresh keys invalidates every live cookie).
pitfalls: Keys are byte slices, not opaque handles: GenerateRandomKey without persistence mints new keys on every restart and silently invalidates all live cookies.

The default gob serializer requires gob.Register for custom types and fails at runtime for unregistered ones; the JSON encoder has its own constraints - pick one and test the round trip of the session type.
Key rotation must be EncodeMulti with the current key and DecodeMulti with current plus previous; a naive swap logs every user out.
securecookie happily produces values larger than a browser accepts - the ~4 KB cookie limit is still yours to enforce.
